citation.title: Parametrization of the Zeeman effect for hydrogen-like spectra in high-temperature plasmas
citation.doi_or_arxiv: PII S0741-3335(02)34785-7 (DOI not printed in supplied text; likely 10.1088/0741-3335/44/7/316, verify)

topic: Spectral line-shape modelling of hydrogen-like impurity CX lines: Zeeman/fine-structure broadening and temperature correction
own_question: How can the unresolved Zeeman and fine-structure pattern be reduced to three Gaussian polarization components for ion-temperature fitting?
actual_method_and_evidence: Exact Zeeman patterns were computed and Gaussians fitted per polarization group. Simple relations were found: σ split ∝B, and the ratio of Zeeman width to Doppler width scales as a power law in T. Parameters are tabulated for 44 transitions, including C VI. Synthetic refits reproduced temperatures typically within 5%. A temperature-dependent centre-wavelength shift was also noted. All evidence is simulation-based, assuming statistical populations; no plasma data validation.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Conventional CES impurity temperatures depend on spectral-fitting choices; neglecting Zeeman/fine-structure broadening inflates apparent temperature, especially at low T.
claim_checks.qualification: Synthetic C VI demonstration; correction magnitude depends on B, T, transition; statistical populations assumed.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not applicable; offline spectrum-model fitting, no nowcasting or timing measurement.
validation_if_relevant: Synthetic refits only; no experimental or held-out data.

reason_to_include_or_exclude: Only optionally cite in background to explain that reported carbon CES temperatures are model-dependent fitted labels; not central to the temporal nowcasting question.
